entities.summary: Li Fuguo, né Li Jingzhong (李靜忠), known from 757 to 758 as Li Huguo (李護國), formally Prince Chou of Bolu (博陸醜王), was a Chinese eunuch, military general, and politician during the reign of Emperor Suzong of the Chinese Tang dynasty. He had served Li Heng while Li Heng was crown prince under Li Heng's father Emperor Xuanzong and later supported Li Heng in ascending the throne during Anshi Rebellion, when Emperor Xuanzong's realm was thrown into confusion. He later became exceedingly powerful, in alliance with Emperor Suzong's wife Empress Zhang, but broke with her and killed her in 762 when Emperor Suzong died.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a key military general and politician during the Anshi Rebellion, Li Fuguo played a crucial role in securing Emperor Suzong's throne, thereby influencing the fate of the Tang dynasty. His actions also led to the downfall of Empress Zhang, who was killed by him in 762.
